clue.text: Speed required in tying this?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a unit of speed at sea, one nautical mile per hour
second meaning: what you make when you tie string or rope

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether haste is needed when tying something up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, more playful half: you need one of these to tie anything at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names the nautical unit of velocity and the loop formed by tying rope.

clue.text: Fool and knave see eye to eye

parts.note: to con someone is to fool them
a cur is a contemptible scoundrel

explanation.surface: A jester and a rogue find themselves in agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to agree, which is the idiom of seeing eye to eye.

clue.text: Monk withdrawing just so rite can change

indicators.note: withdrawing means pulling back, so the phrase before it is read in the backward direction

parts.note: Latin sic, 'thus', marks a quotation as exactly so

indicators.note: letters that change are rearranged into a different order

explanation.surface: A monk retreats so that a religious ceremony can be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just so' is sic, the Latin word editors use to mean 'thus, exactly as written'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cistercian is a member of the strict Benedictine order of monks founded at Cîteaux.

clue.text: Keep mum confined

definitions.meaning: first meaning: stay silent, as a command
second meaning: locked away or enclosed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep mum' looks like looking after a mother; 'mum' here means silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb is both an order to be quiet and a past participle meaning locked in.

clue.text: Special constable starts to take country walks and do some climbing

indicators.note: the first piece starts off the word and the next piece follows it

parts.note: standard abbreviation for a volunteer police officer
to ramble is to walk for pleasure in the countryside

explanation.surface: A volunteer police officer heads off hiking in the hills and does some climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: A special constable is a part-time volunteer officer in British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble is to climb over rough ground using hands as well as feet.

clue.text: Sight site

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to see or catch sight of
second meaning: a place or location

explanation.walkthrough: The two words sound alike, tempting a homophone, but each is a separate meaning of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as a verb for noticing something and a noun for a particular place.

clue.text: Spoil girl in Spanish resort

explanation.surface: Someone pampers a young woman on holiday in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoil' suggests indulging the girl, but it means damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Marbella is a seaside holiday town on Spain's Costa del Sol.

clue.text: Plant used first of all in astringent lotions or embrocations

indicators.note: the first letter of each of all the following words is the one kept

parts.note: initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A plant is the active ingredient in tightening skin creams and rubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant itself turns up in lotions, so the surface is close to literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe is a succulent plant whose sap is used in soothing skin products.

clue.text: Going out to Chile in old age

definitions.note: the noun 'the Neolithic', the later Stone Age

indicators.note: going out suggests letters dispersing and regrouping in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone travels to South America late in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In old age' reads as the elderly traveller, but 'in' belongs to the letters being shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neolithic is the New Stone Age, a prehistoric era, hence an old age of history.

clue.text: Fruit with large stone

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit with a big pip, like a plum or mango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone' seems to be the fruit's seed; it is a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is counted among precious stones and gems in jewellery.

clue.text: In Minnesota citizenship is implied

indicators.note: the answer lies within the run of letters that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the state name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A claim that US citizenship in one state is assumed rather than stated.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is understood without being spoken, so it is implied.

clue.text: Easily managed vehicle reversing on flat surface

indicators.note: a vehicle reversing goes backwards, so its word is read from the end

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle
a table is a flat surface, also a tableland

explanation.surface: A car backs easily onto level ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Tractable means docile and easy to control or handle.

clue.text: Delivery made by down-to-earth supplier

parts.note: surface reading: goods brought by a practical, unpretentious supplier
setter's reading: the supplies literally come down to earth, dropped from an aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down-to-earth' usually means sensible; here it describes cargo falling from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies parachuted or dropped from aircraft are a delivery that travels down to the ground.

clue.text: Racecourse for a person from Kelso, say

parts.note: Kelso is a town in the Scottish Borders

explanation.surface: A racecourse catering to someone from a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is the famous racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Very young cat I lost in the old city

parts.note: baby as an adjective, as in baby carrots

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so that letter is dropped from the word before

explanation.surface: A tiny kitten goes missing in an ancient town.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon was the great city of ancient Mesopotamia.

clue.text: Police wrong to stop little nursery rhyme character

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so this word goes into the middle of the character's name

parts.note: Little Boy Blue, who should come blow his horn

explanation.surface: The police take a wrong step to halt a small figure from children's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' belongs to the rhyme's title, Little Boy Blue, rather than meaning small.
explanation.definitionFit: Boys in blue is an informal phrase for police officers, from their blue uniforms.

clue.text: Silly Billy — name in case of necessity

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name

indicators.note: a case is the outside casing, so only the outermost letters are kept

explanation.surface: A fool is named only if absolutely necessary.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninny is a foolish person, just as a silly billy is.

clue.text: Plants in front of Criterion before start of play

indicators.note: placing one piece before the next sets the order they are joined in
the front of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a play starts with Act I

explanation.surface: Greenery decorates the front of the Criterion, a London theatre, before curtain up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of play' looks like a first letter, but the first part of a play is Act One.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti, the plural of cactus, are spiny desert plants.

clue.text: Pass over Oregon and notice nothing in state

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece over the other means it comes first

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Someone skips Oregon and sees nothing of interest in one state.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is a US state in the Rocky Mountains.

clue.text: Condensation, so we hear, that's expected

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the spelling of the word is swapped for its sound-alike

explanation.surface: A weather remark that some moisture is forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something due is anticipated or scheduled to arrive.

clue.text: Extent to which tides can flow?

indicators.note: flowing water moves things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about how far the tides are able to reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Distance is the extent of space between two points.

clue.text: Long period ending in autumn

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A lengthy stretch of time that finishes in the fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' reads as an adjective for the period; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long for something, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Stories involving National Trust gifts

indicators.note: to involve is to include, so one part is enclosed in the other

parts.note: standard abbreviation for the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: Tales about a heritage charity's donations.
explanation.definitionFit: Talents are natural abilities, often called gifts.

clue.text: Essay about one mathematical function in three volumes?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer word goes round the others

explanation.surface: A piece of writing on a maths topic spanning three books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essay' looks like a written piece but here means an attempt, as in to essay a task.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilogy is a set of three related books or works, hence three volumes.

clue.text: Openers for Australia, maybe, in cricket match providing fewest thrills

indicators.note: these letters sit inside the following word

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

indicators.note: openers are the opening letters of the words that follow

parts.note: initial letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Australia's opening batsmen make a cricket match dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Openers suggests opening batsmen, but it means first letters. A Test match is a full international cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamest is the superlative of tame, meaning dull and least exciting.

clue.text: Girl with land in South America first off

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off and discarded

explanation.surface: A young woman who owns land on that continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivia is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Warner is resolute, seizing genuine article

indicators.note: to seize is to grab hold, so this word wraps round the next pieces

explanation.surface: Someone named Warner stands firm and grabs the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warner' looks like a name, such as the film studio; it is anything that warns.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire alarm is a device that warns of fire, so it is a warner.

clue.text: Don't eat quickly

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a warning against gobbling food; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for abstaining from food and an adverb for rapidly.

clue.text: Girl embracing first of regular soldiers

indicators.note: an embrace wraps around someone, so the name surrounds the letter
only the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A girl hugs the first of the regular troops.
explanation.definitionFit: An army is a body of soldiers organised for land warfare.

clue.text: Cheese is found by female barrister

indicators.note: found beside means set next to, so the pieces are placed side by side

explanation.surface: A woman lawyer comes across some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a barrister's brief is their case papers, and 'brief' is informal for the barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief is British slang for a lawyer, especially a defence barrister.

clue.text: Trees not entirely original

indicators.note: not the whole of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: the first one is the original

explanation.surface: Some trees are not completely native.
explanation.definitionFit: Firs are evergreen coniferous trees.

clue.text: Going astray dooms wicked old city

indicators.note: things going astray wander off course, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: Straying from virtue condemns a sinful ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods at the biblical story itself, where wickedness doomed the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodom is the biblical city destroyed for its sinfulness.

clue.text: Tom Cruise is cast as an outfitter

indicators.note: to cast is also to throw or mould anew, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A film star lands a role playing a clothes supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like film casting, which suits the actor; here it is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A costumier makes or supplies costumes, so is a theatrical outfitter.
